solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Composer of number in brash arrangement

indicators.note: the word in tells us one piece sits inside the other
an arrangement of the word brash means its letters are put in a new order

parts.note: M is the Roman numeral for a thousand, a number

explanation.surface: A musical number written in a showy, brash arrangement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'arrangement' turns BRASH into BRAHS, and 'in' puts M inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Johannes Brahms was a nineteenth-century German composer of symphonies and concertos.

clue.text: It could be a noun, adjective or a verb, perhaps

definitions.text: It could be a noun, adjective or a verb, perhaps

indicators.note: perhaps hints that the two words could be rearranged into another word

explanation.surface: A grammar lesson about a word that can serve as several parts of speech.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' shuffles A VERB, and the result is itself a word that serves as noun, adjective and verb.
explanation.definitionFit: The word serves as a noun (a warrior), an adjective (courageous) and a verb (to confront boldly).

clue.text: Opposed to making a profit — good man!

parts.note: a profit is a gain
ST, saint, is the crossword's good man

explanation.surface: Someone praised as a good man for making a profit, yet set against it.
explanation.definitionFit: Being opposed to something is being set in opposition, synonym for contrary to it.

clue.text: Wandered, heading Middle East instead of west

indicators.note: instead of says one abbreviation takes the place of the other in the word

parts.note: the clue's own first word is reused as the base

explanation.surface: A traveller who roamed, heading to the Middle East rather than going west.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heading' says the swap happens at the front: the first letter W of the clue's own word is replaced by ME.
explanation.definitionFit: To meander is to take a winding, aimless course, a close synonym for roaming.

clue.text: Being without cash is difficult at university

parts.note: difficult means hard
UP is the British idiom for being in residence at university

explanation.surface: A student finds life at university difficult when out of money.
explanation.walkthrough: In British usage a student is 'up' at university, e.g. up at Oxford.
explanation.definitionFit: Hard up is an idiom for short of money, which is being without cash.

clue.text: A backwater that's far from sleepy?

parts.note: a wake is the water left behind a moving boat, water at its back

explanation.surface: A sleepy rural backwater that turns out to be lively.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backwater' usually means a quiet place; here it is the wash behind a vessel.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone wide awake is alert, the opposite of drowsy.

clue.text: Refuse to go through all the cases

definitions.meaning: to turn down an offer politely
in grammar, to list a noun's forms in each grammatical case

explanation.surface: Someone refusing to work through every case on their desk.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both to turn something down and, in Latin grammar, to recite a noun's case endings.

clue.text: Person who makes little effort to move

definitions.text: Person who makes little effort to move

parts.words: Person who makes little effort to move
parts.note: a rider carried in a vehicle travels without effort, and a team member who does not pull their weight is called the same

explanation.surface: A lazy person who can hardly be bothered to stir.
explanation.definitionFit: A traveller in a car or train is carried along, and figuratively a shirker in a team.

clue.text: Moving home

parts.note: reads as relocating house, but means a dwelling that is itself mobile

explanation.surface: A family in the middle of relocating house.
explanation.definitionFit: A trailer towed behind a car is a home on wheels.

clue.text: Body found in the motorist's boot, perhaps

parts.note: a motorist's vehicle is a car
a car's boot is its storage case, its trunk in American English

explanation.surface: A grim discovery of a corpse in a driver's car boot.
explanation.walkthrough: A boot is the British name for a car's trunk.
explanation.definitionFit: A variant spelling of carcass, a dead body.

clue.text: Either rise quickly or don't budge

parts.note: to rise is to stand
fast means quickly

explanation.surface: A choice between leaping up at once or staying put.
explanation.definitionFit: To stand fast is an idiom for holding one's ground firmly.

clue.text: Possibly end a better woman — even a saint!

indicators.note: possibly says the letters of these words might be arranged into another form

explanation.surface: An encouraging remark that a woman might end up better, perhaps even saintly.
explanation.definitionFit: Bernadette is a woman's name, and St Bernadette of Lourdes was a canonised visionary.

clue.text: An almost perfect concept

indicators.note: almost means the word is not quite complete, losing its final letter

parts.note: perfect means ideal

explanation.surface: An almost flawless notion.
explanation.definitionFit: An idea is a notion or thought, a synonym for a concept.

clue.text: Poor shot at route-planning

indicators.note: route-planning suggests working the route out afresh, so its letters are reorganised

explanation.surface: Poor marksmanship when it comes to working out a route.
explanation.walkthrough: In archery or shooting, a hit on the outermost ring of a target scores least.
explanation.definitionFit: A shot striking the outermost ring of a target, the lowest scoring hit, is a poor shot.

clue.text: Love poems are about the same — too much of a good thing

definitions.text: too much of a good thing

parts.note: love is nil in tennis, the letter O

indicators.note: about says the poems go around the other piece

parts.note: poems are verses
DO, short for ditto, means the same

explanation.surface: Love poems all alike, which become tiresome in excess.
explanation.walkthrough: DO is the abbreviation of ditto.
explanation.definitionFit: Overdoses are excessive amounts, idiomatically an excess of something pleasant.

clue.text: They're intended to encourage laying in a little money

definitions.meaning: dummy eggs placed in a hen's nest to coax her to lay
small savings put by for the future

explanation.surface: Inducements to lay down a bit of money in investment.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase names both decoy eggs left in a nest and modest savings put aside.

clue.text: It's not clear how the eggs may be cooked

definitions.meaning: a ... signal or message is garbled and unclear

definitions.text: how the eggs may be cooked
definitions.meaning: eggs beaten and stirred in a pan

explanation.surface: Uncertainty over how breakfast eggs will be prepared.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both garbled beyond understanding and a style of preparing beaten eggs.

clue.text: Got fired, sadly, so sack someone else?

indicators.note: sadly suggests the words are upset into a different order

explanation.surface: A manager who was dismissed and responds by dismissing another.
explanation.definitionFit: To get rid of a person is an idiom for dismissing them from a job.

clue.text: Could it lead to an Anglo-Catholic marriage?

definitions.text: Could it lead to an Anglo-Catholic marriage?

parts.note: Roman as in Roman Catholic
CE, the Church of England, is the English, Anglican church

explanation.surface: A question about whether a love affair might end in a mixed-denomination wedding.
explanation.walkthrough: The Catholic piece comes first: ROMAN then CE, though the clue names Anglo first.
explanation.definitionFit: A love affair, a courtship, may lead to marriage.

clue.text: More mature, so given rent and key, right?

parts.note: a rent is a tear or rip
E is a musical key

explanation.surface: A tenant now grown up enough to be handed the rent book and a key.
explanation.definitionFit: Riper fruit is further ripened, a comparative synonym for more developed.

clue.text: French chemist late on his way up

parts.note: late means past, as in former

indicators.note: in a down clue, up says the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: rue is French for street, a way

explanation.surface: A French scientist running late on his journey northward.
explanation.definitionFit: Louis Pasteur was the French chemist who pioneered pasteurisation and vaccines.

clue.text: A mother for the first orphan?

parts.note: a dam is the mother of an animal

explanation.surface: Seeking a mother for the very first orphaned child.
explanation.definitionFit: In the Bible the first man had no mother, so he was in a sense the first orphan.

clue.text: Disciplinarian marks a test harshly

indicators.note: harshly suggests the words are roughly handled into a new order

explanation.surface: A strict teacher grading an exam severely.
explanation.definitionFit: A taskmaster is a strict overseer who demands hard work, much like a stern enforcer of rules.

clue.text: Persuade agency girl to start task

parts.note: a temp is a temporary worker from an agency

indicators.note: to start points at the opening letter of the following word

explanation.surface: Coaxing a temporary worker to begin a job.
explanation.definitionFit: To tempt is to entice or coax, close to persuading someone.

clue.text: Embarrassed after some hesitation went wrong

indicators.note: after places the first word's piece behind the hesitation

parts.note: er is the sound of hesitating
embarrassed people go red

explanation.surface: Someone flushed after hesitating, having made a mistake.
explanation.definitionFit: To err is to make a mistake, so erred means made a mistake.

clue.text: Chap comes back in new suit, gets big wave

indicators.note: in tells us the chap sits inside the other piece
new says the word suit is remade in a fresh order
comes back means the word is read backwards

parts.note: a chap is a man

explanation.surface: A man returning in a new suit and then caught by a large wave.
explanation.walkthrough: 'comes back', 'new' and 'in' each signal a step; the surface's suit is clothing, not a word to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: A tsunami is a huge sea wave caused by an earthquake.

clue.text: Fast scoring rate

definitions.meaning: a tempo marking written in a musical score

explanation.surface: A batsman's quick run rate in cricket.
explanation.definitionFit: The Italian musical term marks a quick, lively tempo in a score.

clue.text: Bedclothes used as ropes

definitions.meaning: on a sailing boat, the lines that control a sail

explanation.surface: Bedlinen knotted into ropes for an escape.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both bed linen and, in sailing, the lines controlling sails.

clue.text: Worshipped bustle and colour

parts.note: bustle is fuss, ado
red is a colour

explanation.surface: An idol revered with fuss and bright colour.
explanation.definitionFit: Adored means loved deeply, a synonym of venerated.
